Sāyaṇa on 4.33.11: vaḥ yuṣmākaṃ … dhuḥ dadur devāḥ (the gods gave you the Soma drink and its joy at the third pressing); śrāntasya śrāntāt tapoyuktāt ṛte sakhyāya na bhavanti devāḥ (apart from one wearied, joined with austerity, the gods are not for friendship); yata ete śrāntā ato daduḥ (because these toiled, they gave). Both halves of the reading are carried: toil as austerity, gods befriending none without it, and the gift to the Ṛbhus because of their toil. Wilson note 1 reports the same two clauses from Sāyaṇa and remarks that the maxim ‘would seem to apply to the worshipper’; the entry does not claim that. On 4.33.1 Sāyaṇa says the Ṛbhus reached godhead by tapas, consistent. Plain sense: day.js shows 4.33.4 ‘through these their labours they were made immortal’ and 4.33.11, the last verse, names this third libation; ‘Rbhus’ is the app’s spelling. verse.js ok (4.33.11, at [328,11]); entry-check ok on scratch/R2-d044-p.json, 43 words.
